title: Fugaro required-CLI stamp
description: The required-CLI stamp: the node a project publishes at config/policy/required_cli to say the oldest fugaro release that may act on it, written by that installation's own `fugaro update` and read by every project command of every later CLI. It is a fence and not a security boundary (IAM is the boundary), so it never falls, nothing lowers it (D3262) and a reader fails open on every failure except two: a stamp that is present and is not this shape, and a cached value above the running binary that is younger than fifteen minutes (D3264, bounded by D3268). The shape is closed at every level: a member outside these three is refused, because the node is the one thing a CLI below it obeys and a member nobody reads is a decision nobody made. A member is matched exactly, so another case is a member outside this shape and not the one it resembles, and a document carrying a member twice is refused by the decoder, which is the one refusal this schema cannot make. Only a published release writes it (D3269), so a `schema` a reader does not know means the reader is behind and its fix is an upgrade; nothing else here is written by any release, so anything else wrong with the node is a hand edit, whose last-resort recovery is correcting it in the Firebase console (T7). The Go half is internal/versionstamp's Stamp, SchemaVersion, Decode and Encode, and TestSchemaAgreesWithDecode holds the two together in both directions.

schema.$comment: SchemaVersion in internal/versionstamp/stamp.go. A reader refuses a version it does not know rather than reading what it recognises, so this const and that constant move together.

min.description: The oldest fugaro release that may act on this project, as the writer's own Version. Written plainly, without a `v` prefix (A3), and read back through updatecheck.Valid: an optional `v` is accepted here only so a hand edit that adds one is still a version, and Encode drops it. A dev build or a pre-release tag is not a version and is refused.

set_at.description: When the installation's own `fugaro update` wrote the node, in UTC, for the refusal sentence's date. It is what the reader reports to the person as when the fence was raised. A node without it is a hand edit, not a release's write.
